newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish gov wants Riksbank unemployment goal - paper.
newsitem.headline: Swedish gov wants Riksbank unemployment goal - paper.

text.p: Sweden's Social Democratic government and its informal cooperation partner the Centre Party want to set secondary central bank targets for unemployment and growth, business daily Dagens Industri said on Wednesday.
Currently, the Riksbank's only target is price stability, to keep inflation at two percent with an allowed deviation of one percentage point on either side.

The new targets are being discussed among parties which are also deciding if Swedish constitutional law needs to be changed in order to permit Swedish membership in Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU), the newspaper said.

"A majority within the Social Democratic and Centre working groups want to have unemployment and growth as secondary goals," said Peter Eriksson, Green party member of the working group, to the newspaper.
Such targets could mean that the Riksbank would lower its key repurchase rate further. The Riksbank has not lowered the rate this year but cut it to 4.10 percent from 8.91 percent last year.

At present the Riksbank's goals are discussed within the ruling Social Democratic party. Umbrella union group LO argues the central bank must not focus solely on inflation, but must also take account of unemployment and growth.
